title: Oedipus the King, Sophocles
subtitle: 5th century BC AD
subject: litterature
description: Oedipus wants to save Thebes from a plague. As he investigates, he discovers that he himself is the culprit. Sophocles invents the tragedy where to know is to lose oneself.

hero.hook: He's looking for the town's murderer. The murderer is him.

blocks.text: In Athens, in the **5th century BC**, the playwright **Sophocles** created **Oedipus King**. **Aristotle**, Greek philosopher and student of Plato, would later see it as the model of perfect tragedy in his **Poetics**. During an evening at the theater, a king leads an investigation. Each answer brings him closer to the abyss.

The city of **Thebes** is struck by a plague. The **oracle**, response from the gods delivered by the sanctuary of Delphi, asks to punish the murderer of the former king **Laios**. **Oedipus**, current king of Thebes, promises to find it. He doesn't yet know that fate has already placed him at the center of crime.

Before Sophocles, Athenian tragedy was already evolving with **Aeschylus**, the first of the three great tragedies. Sophocles refines the genre: more characters, more psychological tension. He introduces the **tritagonist**, the third actor on stage. On stage, the **choir** accompanies and comments on the action. But the real driving force is man facing what he ignores.

blocks.caption: Oedipus facing the Sphinx: solving the riddle is already entering the trap.

blocks.text: The myth of Oedipus was known before the play. We remember the **Sphinx**, a monster with the head of a woman and the body of a lion. His **ainigma**, the Greek word for “enigma,” asked: “What is the animal that walks on four legs in the morning, two at noon, three in the evening?” » Oedipus replies: the man. He becomes king of Thebes. Sophocles does not surprise by the plot alone. It surprises by the way the hero discovers the truth **in public**, step by step, without being able to stop.

sections.title: The investigation which turns against the investigator

blocks.text: Oedipus questions the soothsayer , a blind prophet of Thebes who sees the past and the future. Then he questions his wife **Jocasta**, widow of Laius. The clues are piling up. The man he killed on a road, the woman he married, the children he had: everything coincides with the oracle he thought he was fleeing by leaving Corinth, the city where he thought he grew up. [[Tiresias]]
Aristotle especially admires two effects in this play: the [[peripeteia]], a brutal reversal of the situation, and the [[anagnorisis]], the moment when Oedipus finally understands who he is.

This is **tragic irony**: the more Oedipus wants to be just and lucid, the more he accelerates his fall. Knowing this doesn't calm you down. It burns. Each question asked in the name of the city brings the king closer to his own condemnation. Sophocles shows that a brilliant intelligence can become the instrument of its own downfall.

sections.title: See too clearly, then get blinded

blocks.text: When the truth comes out, Jocasta commits suicide. Oedipus gouges out his eyes. The king who saw for the city becomes a man who refuses to look at the world. Sophocles ties the [[Destiny and free will in Greek tragedy]]: Oedipus acted freely at every step, and yet each step fulfilled the oracle. Fleeing destiny is sometimes fulfilling it.

blocks.caption: The enigma of the Sphinx: the knowledge that saves Thebes prepares the catastrophe.

blocks.text: The plague, , was not just a disease. It was the religious defilement which strikes a city as punishment for a crime. Oedipus becomes the [[loimos]], scapegoat expelled to purify the city. He leaves Thebes as a beggar, carrying the evil he did not know he had committed. [[pharmakos]]

sections.title: From Freud to our modern investigations

blocks.text: In the 20th century, **Freud**, founder of psychoanalysis, read the [[The Oedipus complex (Freud)]] into the myth. This psychoanalytic concept is very far from Sophocles' reflection on destiny. Beyond psychoanalysis, the play remains the model of the investigation where the detective discovers that he is guilty. Thriller, theater, cinema: the structure still holds.

**Oedipus King** shows that we can want the good of all and destroy our lives by seeking the truth. In Sophocles, seeing clearly is not a victory. It is a test that leaves the city saved, but the man broken.
